name: capacity rehearsal in one 400-word paragraph
markdown: The booking desk can handle the expected morning queue at Linden Hall. We ran a rehearsal during the morning session with the reservation desk using the same arrival order that the hall expects on an ordinary opening day. The entrance team gave each volunteer a printed slip with a made up name and arrival time so that the desk could practice without using anyone's real booking details. We left the normal counter layout in place and had the same number of people on the desk as the opening schedule calls for. In the first window the desk accepted ten reservations. All ten were entered before the window ended and the clerk could find each reservation again by its slip number when the entrance team asked for it. The desk did not need to open a second queue while those ten people were being served. When the next volunteer arrived, the clerk sent the request to the waiting list instead of putting an eleventh reservation into the first window. The volunteer kept the same slip number and the clerk could call that number in order when a place opened later in the session. That handoff is the second thing we wanted to see because the door team needs to be able to tell people where to wait without sending them through the line again. Proof: the booking replay in Files follows the tenth reservation and the first waiting list entry in order. It also records what the clerk said to the volunteer so the entrance team can try the same wording next time. We did not treat the rehearsal as a forecast for a special event because a larger group arriving together could change the time people spend at the desk. The morning result is enough to keep the one queue layout for the usual opening. We erased the practice reservations from the desk book after matching them against the replay. Then we removed the practice waiting list and set out a fresh stack of blank slips. The next shift can start with an empty book instead of having to tell rehearsal names apart from new bookings. We left the usual reference card at the counter and asked the entrance team to keep using the same line for anyone who comes to make a reservation. The replay stays available for anyone who wants to see what happened at the cutoff before the hall opens again on an ordinary morning.
